from pash_annotations.datatypes.BasicDatatypes import Option
from pash_annotations.annotation_generation.annotation_generators.InputOutputInfoGenerator_Interface import InputOutputInfoGeneratorInterface


class InputOutputInfoGeneratorMogrify(InputOutputInfoGeneratorInterface):

    # mogrify (ImageMagick) reads every operand as an image file and, by default, writes
    # the processed image back to the same file (tested: the file is rewritten even when
    # only -identify is given).  Hence operands are both read and overwritten; we mark
    # them as OTHER_OUTPUT, which PaSh treats as side-effectful.
    #
    # Which flags/options affect input/output?
    # -help, -version, -list   -> print to stdout, no image is processed
    # -format TYPE             -> operand is only read; output goes to a sibling file with
    #                             the new suffix (a.png -> a.jpg), which is not on the command
    #                             line, so we keep the operand as OTHER_OUTPUT (over-approximation)
    # -path DIR                -> operand is only read; output goes to DIR/<basename>; DIR is
    #                             typed as a directory output in mogrify.json
    # -write FILE              -> additional output file, typed in mogrify.json
    # -cdl, -clip-mask, -decipher, -encipher, -map, -mask, -profile, -remap, -texture, -tile
    #                          -> files read for configuration, typed in mogrify.json
    # -identify, -print, -verbose -> write to stdout while processing
    # an operand `-` (or `fmt:-`) -> the image is read from stdin and written to stdout
    #
    # Options that take two words (`-morphology method kernel`, `-annotate geometry text`, ...)
    # are not supported by PaSh's parser, which stops at the second word and treats it (and
    # everything after it) as operands.  We repair the case where the two-word option is the
    # last option; otherwise we raise, which makes PaSh treat the command as side-effectful.

    TWO_ARGUMENT_OPTIONS = ["-annotate", "-copy", "-distort", "+distort", "-evaluate", "-floodfill",
                            "-function", "-limit", "-morphology", "+morphology", "-set",
                            "-sparse-color", "+sparse-color", "-statistic"]
    INFO_ONLY_OPTIONS = ["-help", "+help", "-version", "+version", "-list", "+list"]
    STDOUT_OPTIONS = ["-identify", "+identify", "-print", "+print", "-verbose"]

    def generate_info(self) -> None:
        operands_start = self.repair_second_word_of_two_argument_option()
        operand_names = [str(operand.get_name()) for operand in self.cmd_inv.operand_list]
        for name in operand_names[operands_start:]:
            if len(name) > 1 and (name.startswith("-") or name.startswith("+")):
                raise Exception("mogrify: options after a two-argument option are not parsed correctly")

        if self.does_flag_option_list_contain_at_least_one_of(self.INFO_ONLY_OPTIONS):
            # only prints information; no operand is touched
            self.set_implicit_use_of_stdout()
            self.set_all_operands_as_config_arg_type_string()
            return

        if self.does_flag_option_list_contain_at_least_one_of(self.STDOUT_OPTIONS):
            self.set_implicit_use_of_stdout()

        if any(name == "-" or name.endswith(":-") for name in operand_names[operands_start:]):
            # image read from stdin (the operand itself is reported as the stdout output below)
            self.set_implicit_use_of_stdin()

        if self.does_flag_option_list_contain_at_least_one_of(["-path"]) \
                and not self.does_flag_option_list_contain_at_least_one_of(["-format"]):
            # results go to the -path directory, operands are only read
            self.all_operands_are_other_inputs()
        else:
            # results overwrite the operands (or, with -format, a sibling file next to them)
            self.all_operands_are_other_outputs()

        if operands_start == 1:
            # re-apply after the all_operands_* call, which resets every operand
            self.set_first_operand_as_config_arg_type_string()

    def repair_second_word_of_two_argument_option(self) -> int:
        """If the last option takes two words, the first operand is really its second word.
        Returns the index of the first real operand."""
        flag_option_list = self.cmd_inv.flag_option_list
        if len(flag_option_list) > 0 and isinstance(flag_option_list[-1], Option) \
                and flag_option_list[-1].get_name() in self.TWO_ARGUMENT_OPTIONS \
                and self.get_operand_list_length() > 0:
            self.set_first_operand_as_config_arg_type_string()
            return 1
        return 0

class ParallelizabilityInfoGeneratorMogrify(ParallelizabilityInfoGeneratorInterface):

    # mogrify processes each operand (image file) independently and in order: the image is
    # read, all operators are applied, and the result is written back.  Image-sequence
    # operators (-append, -flatten, -layers, ...) act on the frames of one file, never across
    # operands.  Hence the work splits by individual files (IF x SEQ x CONC); the only output
    # stream is what -identify/-print/-verbose write to stdout, one block per file, which
    # concatenation in order reproduces.
    #
    # Which flags/options affect parallelizability?
    # -help, -version, -list   -> nothing is processed, nothing to parallelize
    # -write FILE              -> every copy would write the same file; not parallelized
    # -seed VALUE              -> one random sequence spans all files; separate copies would
    #                             restart it per file; not parallelized
    # -distribute-cache PORT   -> runs a pixel-cache server; not parallelized
    # two-argument options     -> only parallelized when the parse could be repaired (see IO class)
    # operand `-`              -> stdin/stdout image; not parallelized

    TWO_ARGUMENT_OPTIONS = ["-annotate", "-copy", "-distort", "+distort", "-evaluate", "-floodfill",
                            "-function", "-limit", "-morphology", "+morphology", "-set",
                            "-sparse-color", "+sparse-color", "-statistic"]
    NON_PARALLELIZABLE_OPTIONS = ["-help", "+help", "-version", "+version", "-list", "+list",
                                  "-write", "+write", "-seed", "-distribute-cache", "+distribute-cache"]

    def generate_info(self) -> None:
        if self.does_flag_option_list_contain_at_least_one_of(self.NON_PARALLELIZABLE_OPTIONS):
            return
        operand_names = [str(operand.get_name()) for operand in self.cmd_inv.operand_list]
        flag_option_list = self.cmd_inv.flag_option_list
        if len(flag_option_list) > 0 and isinstance(flag_option_list[-1], Option) \
                and flag_option_list[-1].get_name() in self.TWO_ARGUMENT_OPTIONS:
            # the first "operand" is the option's second word
            operand_names = operand_names[1:]
        for name in operand_names:
            if name == "-" or name.endswith(":-"):
                return
            if len(name) > 1 and (name.startswith("-") or name.startswith("+")):
                return  # unparsed options after a two-argument option
        self.append_to_parallelizer_list_if_seq_conc()

content.text:
All four deliverables are written to `output/` and tested. Here is what I did and what I'm unsure about.

## What was produced

- `output/mogrify.py` — one syntax with 488 option nodes (254 `Flag`s, 234 value nodes) and a single positional `Path(arity=ZERO_OR_MORE, dash_as_stdin=True)` for the image files. Enumerated arguments (`-colorspace`, `-compose`, `-gravity`, `-morphology`, …) are `Selection` nodes with the choices taken from `mogrify -list <Type>`; sizes/percentages are `Geometry`, filenames `Path`, `-fx` is `Expression`, `-format` is `Format`.
- `output/annotation/mogrify.json` — the same options in PaSh's table form. File arguments are typed with access kinds: `-cdl -clip-mask -decipher -encipher -map -mask -profile -remap -texture -tile` as `CONFIG_INPUT`, `-write`/`+write` as `FILE OTHER_OUTPUT`, `-path` as `DIR OTHER_OUTPUT`.
- `InputOutputInfoGeneratorMogrify.py` — operands are marked `OTHER_OUTPUT` because mogrify reads and then rewrites each operand in place (I confirmed the file changes even with only `-identify`). With `-path DIR` and no `-format`, operands become read-only inputs and the directory is the output. `-help/-version/-list` only use stdout; `-identify/-print/-verbose` additionally write to stdout; an operand `-` or `fmt:-` reads stdin and writes stdout.
- `ParallelizabilityInfoGeneratorMogrify.py` — since each operand is processed independently, it offers an individual-files splitter with the same command and concatenation, except when `-write` (all copies would write the same file), `-seed` (one random stream spans the files), `-distribute-cache`, info-only options, or a stdin operand is present.

## How it was tested

- Every option, in both `-` and `+` forms, was probed against `/usr/bin/mogrify` to measure how many words it consumes, using a sentinel non-existent image so the result is unambiguous. Fourteen options take two words (`-annotate`, `-copy`, `-distort`, `-evaluate`, `-floodfill`, `-function`, `-limit`, `-morphology`, `-set`, `-sparse-color`, `-statistic`, and the `+` forms of distort/morphology/sparse-color).
- I/O behaviour (in-place rewrite, `-format`, `-path`, `-write`, `-` on stdin/stdout, which options print) was verified with real PNG files.
- The annotation files were loaded into a scratch copy of the real `pash_annotations` 0.2.4 package (fetched from PyPI as a package installer would) and run over 20 invocations; all parse and classify as intended. `caruca` is not on PyPI, so `mogrify.py` was only import-checked against a stub of `caruca.ir.syntax` that accepts the documented constructor keywords.

## Things to be aware of

1. **Man page vs. binary.** Eleven documented options are rejected by this build as "unrecognized option": `-adjoin`, `-affinity`, `-bench`, `-clip-path`, `-fft`, `-ift`, `-insert`, `-linear-stretch`, `-ping`, `-preview`, `-red-primary`. I left them out. Conversely, eight undocumented options are accepted and included: `-noop`, `-concurrent`, `-average`, `-box`, `-map`, `-duration`, `-metric`, `-rotational-blur`.
2. **Two-word options have no native representation** in either format. In `mogrify.py` the node carries the first word's type and a comment; a side variable `mogrify_two_argument_options` gives the second word's type. PaSh's parser stops at the second word, so the generators repair the case where such an option is the *last* option (the first "operand" is reclassified as a string); if other options follow it, the I/O generator raises, which PaSh treats as side-effectful. `-set` and `-limit` after other options are the most likely real-world casualties.
3. **`-format` outputs are not representable.** `mogrify -format jpg a.png` creates `a.jpg`, which is not on the command line, so the operand stays `OTHER_OUTPUT` as a conservative over-approximation.
4. **Colours and floats** have no vocabulary entry, so colours are `String` and floating-point values are `Other`. ImageMagick enum matching is case-insensitive, which `Selection.choices` can't express; `-channel` accepts combinations like `RGBA`, so it is a `String`.
5. Both `-X` and `+X` are listed as distinct options (not aliases), since their meaning differs; `+X` usually takes no argument where `-X` takes one, and that was verified per option.
